<!-- codex-wake-plan0216-efficient-observation-spec -->

## Problem Statement

Smart tabs are sluggish and lose useful status because the current observer
reconstructs pane/process/session evidence repeatedly. Updates and rollback have
exceeded workspace deadlines; expired display evidence previously produced STALE
labels and unwanted dimming. Operators need prompt activity and meaningful health
without sacrificing terminal responsiveness or changing stock harnesses.

## Solution

A shared host-owned observer maintains bounded, identity-qualified cached evidence,
consumes passive terminal/Codex changes where supported, reconciles cheaply when
needed, and updates only changed tabs. Activity, exact responsiveness and visible
errors remain independent. Appearance stays steady when sources are unavailable;
uncertain activity cues disappear and inspection explains why. Existing presets,
rollback, accounts and live conversations remain independent and preserved.

## User Stories

1. As an operator, I want running/idle/waiting changes to appear promptly, so I can identify active work.
2. As an operator, I want roughly one-second updates and p95 no worse than two seconds on qualified event paths, so tabs are useful while work progresses.
3. As an operator, I want 100 tabs across sessions/accounts supported within measured budgets, so monitoring does not become another resource problem.
4. As an operator, I want shared observers instead of per-tab processes, so cost stays bounded.
5. As an operator, I want stock Byobu/tmux to remain unchanged, so ordinary terminals keep working.
6. As an operator, I want stock Codex and independent sessions preserved, so observation cannot interrupt conversations.
7. As an operator, I want exact responsiveness checks independent of activity, so a busy daemon is not mistaken for a responsive TUI.
8. As an operator, I want immediate bounded explicit health inquiries, so I can investigate suspected problems.
9. As an operator, I want background health no more frequently than once per minute per agent, so routine painting is inexpensive.
10. As an operator, I want visible errors detected in about five seconds on supported active/changed tabs, so actionable failures are noticed.
11. As an operator, I want error text classified locally and redacted, so raw screens/drafts/history are not retained.
12. As an operator, I want errors cleared only by fresh resolution/absence evidence, so failed checks cannot hide errors.
13. As an operator, I want palette/name/stable type preserved on source loss, so a broken connection does not change my theme.
14. As an operator, I want uncertain activity/attention cues removed quietly, so stale RUN or error indications are not presented as current.
15. As an operator, I want no repeated STALE label or whole-tab freshness dimming, so tabs remain compact and legible.
16. As an operator, I want a quiet long-running turn to remain active while its qualified source remains valid, so elapsed time alone cannot invent inactivity.
17. As an operator, I want automatic reconnect and bounded fallback, so temporary outages recover without manual process work.
18. As an operator, I want reused PID/pane/window/thread identities fenced, so a replacement never inherits another session's evidence.
19. As an operator, I want fair background scheduling and coalesced changes, so event bursts do not starve quieter tabs.
20. As an operator, I want skipped/overloaded work reported as unknown/degraded, so the resource cap cannot silently fabricate freshness.
21. As an operator, I want the observer to survive client disconnects, so monitoring is not tied to one terminal view.
22. As an operator, I want independent activity/health/error switches, so expensive checks can be controlled without losing my palette.
23. As an operator, I want pause/resume separate from formatting rollback, so stopping checks need not erase my display preference.
24. As an operator, I want one-command original-settings rollback and reenable, so experiments stay reversible.
25. As an operator, I want readable observer status and equivalent JSON/API/MCP, so troubleshooting needs no opaque IDs.
26. As an operator, I want counters for source/cache/backlog/cost and uncertainty reasons, so performance and evidence are inspectable.
27. As an operator, I want resource caps measured including owned workers, so hidden subprocess costs cannot escape accounting.
28. As an operator, I want qualified WSL Codex events first with existing Grok/SSH/psmux capabilities preserved, so progress does not imply false cross-harness parity.
29. As an operator, I want source/fixture/installed/live acceptance kept distinct, so a passing simulation is not sold as a working deployment.
30. As an operator, I want validation without synthetic provider requests, agent restarts or input, so qualification cannot disrupt my work.

## Implementation Decisions

- One persistent host observation owner, bounded source adapters and worker pool;
  no per-tab daemon or MCP server. Collect process/pane facts once and enrich the
  same identity-bound observations; retain stat/birth/generation-qualified caches.
- Native Codex adapter uses existing metadata/status broadcasts. Terminal adapter
  uses metadata-only control mode with output disabled and no resize/detach/input.
  All external methods/commands are finite allowlisted read-only observation.
- Establish bounded baselines before deltas; reconnect creates a new source epoch.
  Sequence gaps, process replacement and namespace mismatch invalidate affected
  evidence until reconciliation. Do not resume threads to subscribe to activity.
- Never replay an uncertain mutation; observation itself grants no control/input
  custody, enrollment, model execution or recovery authority.
- Cheap fallback metadata reconciliation and dirty-tab projection are independent
  of deep responsiveness and guarded visible-error checks. Rendering reads cache;
  no health RPC or binary hashing is required for an unchanged display tick.
- Health background cadence is at least60seconds per exact agent; explicit requests
  bypass background cadence but remain bounded. Error observation targets five
  seconds for qualified active/dirty sources, slower fallback reported honestly.
- Resource acceptance at100tabs: steady idle <=1% of one CPU core, ordinary active
  <=5% of one core, each over60seconds; aggregate incremental observer RSS<=256MiB
  including owned workers. Cold start measured separately. Ordinary active fixture
  uses ten concurrently active conversations with staggered state changes every
  five seconds, plus bounded coalescing/reconnect-burst cases. These fixture
  assumptions are recorded and do not replace live host measurement.
- Event latency target roughly1second/p95<=2seconds from event receipt to public
  projection on qualified paths. Bound queue length, coalesce superseded state,
  prioritize changed/active tabs and rotate slow work fairly; expose drops/gaps.
- Stable labels/palette never expire because an observation is old. Source loss
  removes uncertain activity/attention without blanket dimming or STALE text.
  Retain last-known redacted detail and separate freshness/source availability.
- Persist owner/configuration and rollback custody; derived observation state may
  be bounded/coalesced and never becomes action authority. Reconnect automatically
  when monitoring enabled; stop/pause affects observation, not agents/palette.
- Existing monitor/controller CLI/API/MCP remain canonical. Add independently
  configurable tiers and readable status; keep machine JSON and exact diagnostics.
- First qualification is WSL stock Byobu/tmux and stock/modded Codex. Existing
  Grok/SSH/psmux behavior remains explicit supported/unknown fallback. Future event
  adapters require independent acceptance; no new Windows service or harness mod.
- Private100tab and existing44+tab read-only live measurements precede automatic
  production enablement; report receipts and any budget failure. Implementation
  delivery is a validated branch, not permission to merge/deploy/start production.

## Testing Decisions

- Existing public controller/monitor operations prove cached inventory, lifecycle,
  tier switches, diagnostics, fallback and recovery. External native adapter seams
  prove actual protocol framing, read-only method/command sets, epoch sequencing
  and ownership; use private native/transport fixtures, not mocks of internals.
- Native tmux tests prove no focus/size/layout/input/agent changes, lost-source
  quiet rendering, dirty-only effects and original baseline rollback.
- Golden worked identities prove PID/window/thread replacement and reconnect
  cannot borrow evidence. Inject clocks at time boundaries for fair schedules,
  expiry and bounded explicit health without sleeps or forged freshness.
- Exact immutable installed package proves CLI, actual stdio MCP, authenticated
  API/OAuth MCP where these operations already exist, and generated help/completion.
- Measure100tab idle/ordinary-active60second windows, CPU ticks, whole owned-tree
  RSS, child census, source calls, hashes, captures, native writes and event p95.
  Record startup separately, preserve first failures and fixed thresholds.
- Read-only existing-host acceptance must not change production layouts/themes,
  inject text, start model turns, restart agents or retain raw screen content.
  Final fresh OS/resource census verifies owned fixture cleanup.
- Local checks on Python3.11/3.12 replace paid hosted CI. One broad Standards/Spec
  review after ticket closure and one bounded TDD remediation pass; no repeat loop.

## Out of Scope

New model work, prompt delivery, session migration, native harness modifications,
modified Byobu, Windows-native service hosting, new external OAuth exposure,
raw terminal/history storage, production deployment or automatic monitor enablement
before separate qualified activation. Existing account/grant/resource controls stay.

## Further Notes

All15 interview decisions accepted and consolidated understanding confirmed by
explicit direction to publish/implement. The agreed existing public seams are
reused; external source adapters add only bounded observation seams. Exact scope,
worker ownership, blockers, test budgets and review counters live in the execution
ledger. Parent discussion remains open; close implementation tickets only from
integrated acceptance evidence.
